summary: The paper studies three training-free uncertainty-quantification signals (mean-max-prob, negative predictive entropy, self-consistency), a logistic combination, and a hidden-state probe for predicting correctness of a tiny (~50K-parameter) from-scratch transformer trained on integer addition, using exact ground truth to avoid the LLM-judge confound present in most open-domain UQ evaluations. This revision adds a 2,000-resample bootstrap CI on the main seed's AUROC gaps (showing mean-max-prob significantly beats self-consistency but not entropy) and a per-difficulty AUROC breakdown, while candidly flagging that a multi-seed sweep at the main run's own 65%-accuracy operating point — requested by all three prior review rounds — is still not done.
strengths:
- I reran experiment.py end-to-end (PyTorch 2.12.1+cpu, ~294s) and every reported number reproduced exactly: overall accuracy 0.6535, AUROC 0.8712/0.8631/0.8408/0.8742 for mean-max-prob/entropy/self-consistency/logistic-combo, the bootstrap CIs (e.g. mmp-vs-sc gap 0.0301 [0.0124, 0.0487], excludes zero; mmp-vs-nme gap 0.0083 [-0.0007, 0.0175], includes zero), the per-digit AUROC breakdown, ECE values, and the risk-coverage figures (81.0% accuracy at 70% coverage, 87.8%/90.6% at 55%/50% coverage) — the paper's central claims are not just plausible but bit-for-bit verified against the included code.
- The controlled, ground-truth-exact setup is a genuinely clean way to isolate UQ-signal quality from judge quality, and the paper is explicit and correct about the scope limitation (absolute numbers should not transfer to frontier LLMs) rather than overclaiming generality.
- Unusually transparent revision process: rather than hand-waving away the still-open seed-stability question with generic "future work" language, the paper states exactly what was traded off (bootstrap CI + per-digit breakdown vs. a ~1,200s multi-seed sweep) and why, which makes the paper's own claims easier to calibrate trust against.
weaknesses:
- The central request repeated across all three prior rounds — a multi-seed sweep at the main run's own ~65%-accuracy scale — is still not done in this revision. The new bootstrap CI is a within-seed sampling-noise estimate over one trained model's held-out predictions; it does not speak to whether a different training seed at the same accuracy would preserve the mean-max-prob > self-consistency ranking or the calibration numbers, which is the more consequential form of variance for a paper whose second sentence is about generalizing a signal comparison. After four rounds, this remains the single largest unresolved rigor gap in the paper's own headline claim.
- The two existing multi-seed sweeps (reduced-scale ~3% accuracy, mid-scale ~31% accuracy) confound accuracy with training-set size, epoch count, and test-set size simultaneously (acknowledged explicitly in Sections 3 and 4), so the claim that self-consistency's instability is "largely an artifact of the near-degenerate low-accuracy regime" is not actually isolated from a competing explanation (larger test set alone stabilizing the AUROC estimate) — the paper is honest about this but it does undercut how much weight that result can carry.
- The per-digit AUROC finding (worst discrimination at 2-3 digits rather than the hardest 4-digit bucket) is presented as a real pattern but is only computed on a single seed with n≈250 per bucket and no CI is given for the by-digit breakdown (only for the aggregate AUROCs), so it isn't clear whether the non-monotonicity itself is distinguishable from noise.
questions:
1. Given that the reduced- and mid-scale sweeps already exist, would fixing test-set size across both (subsample the mid-scale test set down to 400) let you isolate the accuracy effect from the test-size effect on self-consistency's variance without a full new training run?
2. For the per-digit AUROC breakdown, can you get a bootstrap CI within each digit bucket (reusing the same resampling machinery already implemented) to establish whether the 2-3 digit dip is statistically distinguishable from the 1-digit and 4-digit values, given n≈250 per bucket?
3. If a full 65%-accuracy multi-seed sweep is out of budget this round, would even 2 extra seeds (rather than the ideal 5) be affordable, to at least bound whether the headline AUROC ranking is seed-fragile at the paper's actual operating point?
